idiom_name: net/http method+path patterns on a /v1 prefix + compiler-enforced internal/ packages
implementation_notes: Go publishes the protocol as a package of handlers plus the request/response structs that carry the shapes; since Go 1.22 the standard ServeMux understands method-and-wildcard patterns, so mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/orders", ...) is versioned routing without a third-party router. The 'keep internals private' half of the pattern is enforced by the compiler rather than by discipline: packages under internal/ can only be imported from within the same module subtree, so consumers physically cannot reach the domain packages, and the exported API package is the published contract. Remote consumers get the same contract from a .proto with grpc-go, and module major-version suffixes (/v2) carry the protocol version in the import path for library-shaped consumers.
pitfalls: Exported-field names and json tags are the contract: renaming a field or dropping a tag is a breaking wire change even though the code compiles.
json.Decoder ignores unknown fields, which helps additive evolution but also hides consumer typos; validate DTOs explicitly (DisallowUnknownFields or a schema check) where that matters.
Handler state shared across goroutines (maps, counters, buffers) races under load - keep per-request state local and guard shared state with explicit synchronisation.
